decisions.reason: Although management may hesitate because the service has remained on the website since 2023, it is far from the firm’s maritime strategy, lacks visible success signals, and is the easiest offering to cut if focus returns to core integrated shipping services.

This service extends the firm’s established crewing capabilities into an adjacent segment, so despite limited public evidence of results, its strategic fit and prior commitment make continued support more likely than withdrawal.

The maritime education programme is highly consistent with the firm’s training network, was launched publicly in 2024, and already shows early partner traction, which encourages management to continue rather than reverse course.

Emissions monitoring and compliance services sit close to the core offer, match the stated push toward environmental performance, and have a clearly communicated implementation success, making withdrawal very unlikely.

The emissions compliance dashboard supports the firm’s digitalisation and compliance agenda and is integrated into its PAL software, so sunk development effort and strategic visibility strongly favor keeping it on the market.

The emissions compliance cost simulation tool is also embedded in the firm’s software and fits its environmental advisory direction, so management is likely to persist with it while attributing any weak uptake to the newness of FuelEU-related demand.
